name: Arsenic trioxide
route_note: IV infusion daily during induction and on a schedule during consolidation; oral formulations are used in China and studied elsewhere
originator: Harbin Medical University (Zhang Tingdong) and Shanghai Institute of Hematology (Chen Zhu, Wang Zhenyi); Western development by Cell Therapeutics

discovery.by: Zhang Tingdong and colleagues, Harbin Medical University
discovery.note: Investigated arsenic-containing traditional remedies; reported activity of arsenic trioxide (Ailing-1) in APL in the 1970s–1990s.

tagline: Ancient poison repurposed as a curative, chemotherapy-free treatment for APL
summary: Arsenic trioxide is an inorganic compound that binds the PML portion of the PML::RARA oncoprotein and triggers its degradation, inducing differentiation and apoptosis of leukaemic promyelocytes. With tretinoin, it allows chemotherapy-free cure of most patients with acute promyelocytic leukaemia.
mechanism: Trivalent arsenic binds cysteine residues in the B-box/RING domain of PML, causing oligomerisation, SUMOylation by UBC9 and RNF4-mediated ubiquitination, and proteasomal degradation of both PML and the PML::RARA fusion.

Loss of the fusion relieves the block on myeloid differentiation and restores PML nuclear bodies; at higher concentrations arsenic also induces oxidative stress and apoptosis. Tretinoin acts on the RARA moiety, so the two agents are synergistic.
uses: Acute promyelocytic leukaemia: first-line in low-risk disease with tretinoin
Relapsed or refractory APL after tretinoin and anthracycline therapy

history.title: Harbin studies
history.detail: Physicians at Harbin Medical University begin using arsenic-containing preparations for leukaemia.

history.title: APL results
history.detail: Harbin investigators report high remission rates in APL with intravenous arsenic trioxide.

history.title: Mechanism
history.detail: Shanghai investigators (Chen Guo-Qiang, Chen Zhu and colleagues) show arsenic induces apoptosis and degrades PML::RARA.

history.title: US trial
history.detail: Soignet et al. at Memorial Sloan Kettering report remissions in relapsed APL (NEJM).

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved as Trisenox for relapsed or refractory APL.

history.title: Direct target
history.detail: Zhang et al. (Science) show arsenic binds PML zinc fingers directly.

history.title: APL0406
history.detail: ATRA plus arsenic trioxide proves superior to ATRA plus chemotherapy in low/intermediate-risk APL.

history.title: First-line approval
history.detail: FDA approves Trisenox with tretinoin for newly diagnosed low-risk APL.

pk.half_life: arsenious acid about 10–14 hours; methylated metabolites longer

serious: QT prolongation and torsades de pointes
safety.boxed_warning: Boxed warning for differentiation syndrome and cardiac conduction abnormalities (QT prolongation, torsades de pointes); later labels add encephalopathy warnings.

facts: Arsenic compounds were used medicinally for centuries, including Fowler's solution, a 19th-century treatment for leukaemia.
